title: CDMA Walsh-coded wordlines read many gain cells at once
idea: Borrowed from cellular CDMA: N nondestructive gain cells on one bitline are activated together, each wordline modulated by an orthogonal Walsh code across N short read slots. One integrating sense block despreads the summed bitline current into N bits.
why: Periphery per bit: one sense block serves 8-16 cells per access with ~sqrt(N) noise processing gain, cutting sense amps ~4-8x in gain-cell arrays.

title: Floating-gate offset trim written into each sense amp at test
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x trimmed latch x planar x bulk Si x one added embedded-floating-gate mask. Each SA includes a small floating-gate transistor programmed at wafer sort to null its measured Vt mismatch, cutting input-referred offset from ~20 mV to ~2-3 mV.
why: Lower offset allows 2x longer bitlines (half the SAs, periphery -10% of die) or a 2x smaller Cs.

title: Retired sense-amp stripes reborn as bit-serial compute engines
idea: Ideal result: periphery that finds a second job. Design SA stripes with a bit-serial logic mode (multi-row activation for AND/OR plus a latch-side XOR), so dies retired for poor retention are reused as in-memory compute engines with short data lifetimes.
why: Recyclability: a second-life market for degraded dies, and fewer data-movement joules (fact 5) for bulk bitwise work.

title: Po: the bit is when, not how much — wordline ramp
idea: Po: memory read by timing. Ramp the wordline slowly: an access transistor holding '0' turns on near Vwl=Vt while one holding '1' turns on only near Vt+VDD/2, so a per-bitline edge detector timestamps the first bitline movement against the ramp and decodes data from turn-on time and direction, largely independent of Cs.
why: Capacitor wall (#1): sensing becomes tolerant of small and variable Cs (~2 fF cells), and slow wordline edges reduce coupling disturbance (row hammer #9).

title: Token-ring wordline selection for streaming-mode DRAM banks
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x standard SA x shift-register wordline selection x bulk Si x standard flow. In AI-weight and KV-cache streaming banks, a one-hot token passed along a shift register selects successive rows, with only coarse 64-row-block decoding for random jumps, replacing full in-pitch row decoders.
why: Row decoder area -70-80% in streaming banks; lower activation energy for sequential reads.

title: Jacquard warp-weft coincident wordline selection replaces tree decoders
idea: Borrow the Jacquard loom, where a hook lifts only where card and lifting bar coincide: each sub-wordline driver is a two-input threshold switch at the crossing of a 'warp' line (high address bits, sqrt(N) lines) and a 'weft' line (low bits, sqrt(N) lines). Each line supplies only half the boost charge, so half-selected drivers stay below threshold and only the doubly-selected wordline fires.
why: Cuts decoder transistors per wordline from ~6-10 to ~2 and predecode routing from O(log N) tracks per row to O(sqrt N) per mat: ~40-60% row-decoder area reduction.

title: Cicada prime-period refresh jitter defeating hammer synchronization
idea: Periodical cicadas emerge on prime cycles (13, 17 years) so predators cannot sync with them. Controller firmware schedules REF commands per bank at co-prime, jittered intervals within DDR5's postpone/pull-in allowance (mean stays tREFI). Neither workloads nor attackers can then phase-lock activations to in-DRAM TRR sampling windows. Firmware plus FPGA tests, ~$250k in 12 months.
why: Fact 9: synchronization-based patterns defeat TRR. Desynchronizing restores TRR effectiveness with zero die area.

title: Eliminate silicon wafers for periphery: LTPS-on-glass panels from display fabs
idea: Build DRAM periphery as laser-crystallized LTPS CMOS on Gen-6 glass in underused LCD/OLED fabs converted to wet etches (H3PO4/HNO3/acetic, oxalic) and Cl-only dry etch, with fluorine chamber cleans replaced by Cl2/O2. Dice the panels into tiles and bond them face-to-face over array dies at 2-5 um pitch through mux-concentrated bitline groups.
why: Display-fab area costs ~1/10 of silicon fab area, and LTPS mobility (~100 cm2/Vs) handles 200-400 MHz periphery, so periphery capital and cost per die fall sharply.

title: Hydro cascade: voltage-stacked global I/O lanes reuse current
idea: A river turns two mill wheels in series. Two internal global data-line domains are stacked between VDD and ground, one swinging VDD to VDD/2 and the other VDD/2 to ground, so the same charge drives both before reaching ground; a small balancer absorbs mismatch.
why: Halves internal global I/O energy, a big share of DRAM's 10-20 pJ/bit (fact 5), with external DQ unchanged.

title: Metal-contact NEMS relays power-gate mats and steer redundancy
idea: Mechanical relays have zero leakage and no oxide or junction to degrade at 125 C; their endurance limit (~1e10 cycles) is only a problem for fast paths. Use BEOL NEMS relays for mat power gating and redundancy steering, which switch only at boot or idle transitions.
why: Periphery standby leakage at hot -> ~0; relays sit above silicon, freeing area (fact 7).

title: Virtual Channel Memory reborn as BEOL shadow row buffers
idea: Failure mined: NEC's Virtual Channel SDRAM added SRAM channel buffers between the sense amps and I/O but died on area cost and standards politics. Fix: stack 4-8 extra row buffers as BEOL oxide-transistor 2T dynamic latches directly above the SA stripe, at zero silicon area, so each bank keeps several rows open.
why: Overfetch and activation (facts 8, 9): higher row-hit rates cut activations 2-3x, and activation energy and row-hammer exposure fall in proportion.

title: Core-memory coincident selection with threshold-switch row drivers
idea: Revive magnetic core memory's coincident-current trick: each local wordline driver is gated by a two-terminal ovonic threshold switch fed by one X and one Y predecode line, each at half threshold. Only the row where both are active fires its driver, replacing NAND decode trees.
why: Periphery area: row-decoder transistor count falls ~4x (decoders ~8-10% of die to ~3%); the OTS is BEOL-compatible.

title: Display-fab turnkey lines for U.S. memory periphery
idea: Borrowed from the solar and display industries' turnkey-line model: buy standard Gen-6 glass toolsets (flat-panel i-line steppers, PECVD, sputter) and run memory panels with relaxed 1-2 um periphery rules, since glass area costs ~100x less than wafer area, sited in the U.S. within ~18-24 months.
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability: periphery capex per m2 ~10x below a DRAM fab, with no EUV and no quartz crucibles.

title: Eliminate the restore phase: consume-on-read memory for single-use data
idea: Add a destructive-read command and 'read-once' regions whose sense amps never write back. Activations, gradient buffers, evicted KV entries and packets are read once, then the row is marked free, so the SA fires at low swing and the row closes right after the burst.
why: Restore is ~40-50% of row-cycle energy and tRAS (fact 8). For read-once traffic (~30-50% of accelerator traffic), row energy falls ~40% and bank occupancy ~35%, so fewer bits are needed per unit of throughput.

title: Composite: silicon sense chiplets mass-transferred onto glass DRAM panels
idea: TRIZ #40 Composite: large glass panels carry stacked oxide-TFT DRAM tiers, while all precision sensing lives in 50x50 um silicon sense chiplets placed every few millimetres by micro-LED-style mass transfer (millions per hour) and wired by panel redistribution layers; glass does storage, silicon does amplification.
why: 100x path: panel processing costs ~$100-300/m2 versus ~$100k/m2 for EUV DRAM wafers, so with ~0.3 um panel nanoimprint and 16-32 TFT tiers it aims at ~$0.1-0.5/GB; trade-offs: bulky modules, ~us latency and higher energy. Speculative because panel lithography must improve ~5x. Attacks Facts 4 and 7.

title: Ferroelectric HZO negative-capacitance shunt minifies effective bitline capacitance
idea: A thin HZO film (crystallized at 350-400 C) in a capacitor shunted to each bitline segment is biased in its negative-capacitance region during charge sharing, MINIFYING the net bitline capacitance by 50-70%.
why: Fact 1: signal 2-3x, enabling ~2x smaller Cs or VARY ~0.6 V; hysteresis-free transient NC at ns speed is unproven, hence high risk.

title: Charge-transfer preamplifier revived with one low-Vt implant
idea: The charge-transfer sense schemes of 1970s DRAMs moved bitline charge through a near-threshold transistor onto a tiny node. One added low-Vt implant mask makes pitch-matched transfer gates that, biased at threshold, pass the cell's signal charge from a ~60 fF bitline onto a ~4 fF node, multiplying voltage swing ~5-10x before the latch.
why: Large signal gain (fact 1) permits 3D DRAM tiers with ~1-2 fF capacitors (fact 2) or 2-4x longer bitlines with fewer sense amps (fact 7).

title: Varactor-state cell read by reactance without removing charge
idea: Store the bit on a MOS capacitor biased so '1' is accumulation (high C) and '0' depletion (low C); read with a small AC probe through the access device and measure the reactance in a bridge, which moves no net charge off the cell. Measuring a reactive parameter costs ~zero dissipated energy in the ideal limit.
why: Non-destructive read removes restore energy and page overfetch (fact 8); also lengthens effective retention because reads stop disturbing cells.

title: Lateral-BJT sense amplifier on open 130 nm PDK gain-cell macro
idea: Effect: Boltzmann-diffusion matching of bipolar Vbe. A small team designs a gain-cell memory macro on a SkyWater/GF open-PDK MPW whose sense amp is a differential pair of parasitic vertical/lateral BJTs. Vbe mismatch is ~0.5-1 mV versus ~10-20 mV for small MOSFETs, so tiny 2T/3T gain-cell read currents are resolved by a small, untrimmed stage.
why: Sense margin and U.S. manufacturability: 512+ cells per SA and lower read currents (longer retention) in a U.S. 130 nm fab, designed fabless.

title: Postal routing: packet-switched mats replace global decoders
idea: A postal worker sorts by zip code at each hub instead of reading one master list. Replace global row/column decoders and wide global I/O buses with a small on-die mesh: address and data packets hop to mats, each mat decodes locally, and replies return as packets.
why: Shrinks global wiring and decoders (part of fact 7's 49%) and lets many small sub-mat accesses run concurrently, cutting overfetch (fact 8).

title: Multi-row OR-sensing reads sparse zero blocks in one activation
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x threshold-OR sensing x 8-wordline simultaneous activation x bulk Si x standard. For sparse activations and pruned weights, eight rows open at once and the SA only asks whether any charge is present (group testing); all-zero groups are confirmed with one sense instead of eight, and the extra multi-row disturb (<1%) is tolerated.
why: Sense energy and overfetch for sparse data cut up to 8x, spending the 1% budget on multi-row disturb.

title: Open-source DRAM periphery IP library on a U.S. foundry
idea: Worse: keep sense-amp, decoder and pump know-how locked inside three companies. Flip: a federally funded consortium publishes silicon-proven sense amps, wordline drivers, charge pumps and test macros on a U.S. mature node, so startups pairing novel cells with standard periphery need not reinvent it.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital intensity: removes years of periphery design time and cost for new entrants.

title: Parametric varactor amplification boosts bitline voltage after charge sharing
idea: Box: stacked cap x Si access x parametric amplification x MOS-varactor bitline segments x bulk Si x standard. After the cell shares charge onto the bitline, a pump pulse drives MOS varactors on the bitline pair into depletion, shrinking capacitance so V = Q/C and the differential rise 3-5x before the latch fires: low-noise gain from capacitance modulation.
why: 3-5x more signal without more Cs: shrink the capacitor or lengthen bitlines.

title: Truncated restore: shorten write-back, accept 1% under-restored cells
idea: Box: standard cap x Si access x early-terminated restore x standard x bulk Si x standard. After the destructive read the SA stops restoring at ~70% of full level, cutting tRAS/tRC ~30%; the few cells left too weak for the next read fall inside the code budget, and refresh tops them up.
why: Destructive-read cost: row cycle time ~-30%, higher bank throughput, less energy per activation.

title: Tuning fork: analog trim cell retunes every sense amp offset
idea: Like filing a tuning fork to pitch, each SA gets one DRAM-style trim capacitor on its tail node; at power-up and then every refresh window the bitlines are shorted and a calibration loop pumps charge onto that cap until the latch flips at zero input, so the offset correction is stored as analog charge and refreshed like data.
why: Periphery area: SA devices are upsized only to beat Pelgrom mismatch; nulling ~80% of offset lets them shrink ~4x in area (SA strip ~25-35% smaller) or halves the bitline signal needed, easing the capacitor wall.

title: Stochastically assembled nanowire decoders with post-fab calibration map
idea: Box: crossbar-pitch storage x nanowire access x conventional SA x self-assembled sub-litho lines x Si x DSA patterning. A few lithographic mesowires address sub-lithographic lines through randomly doped regions, and a built-in calibration pass discovers each line's code and stores it in a lookup, so decoders need no litho pitch matching.
why: Decoders scale below litho pitch without EUV; decoder area ~-70% and fewer EUV layers.

title: Polarity-swapping sense amps balance BTI aging to shrink offset margins
idea: Effect: bias-temperature instability (NBTI/PBTI) threshold drift. Every refresh epoch, a swap network flips which half of each SA pair connects to the true versus complement bitline (data stored inverted, one flag per mat), so BTI shifts build up equally on both transistors and cancel instead of growing into offset.
why: SA area (fact 7): reclaims the end-of-life offset margin (often ~30% of the budget), allowing smaller SA devices or longer bitlines; a pure design change on MPW.

title: Fe: iron-core inductors resonantly recycle bitline precharge energy
idea: Give each bank an on-die inductor with an electroplated Fe-Ni magnetic core; when sensing finishes, bitline charge is swung through LC resonance into the next bank's precharge instead of being dumped to the half-VDD rail, recovering roughly half of the CV2.
why: Attacks the voltage-floor CV2 energy (fact 10) of activate/precharge; claims 30-50% lower array activation energy.

title: Pitch-split: off-pitch periphery moves to U.S. 200mm chiplets
idea: Rearrange periphery by pitch-criticality: only bitline SAs and sub-wordline drivers stay on the array die from a U.S. memory fab; pumps, regulators, DLL, I/O, ESD, command logic, test and fuses move to a chiplet from U.S. 200mm/130-65 nm lines, attached face-to-face at a U.S. OSAT such as Amkor Arizona.
why: Fact 7 and capital: ~20-25% of die area returns to cells; the off-pitch half runs on fully depreciated U.S. fabs with zero EUV.

title: Margin-binned short-refresh SKU rescues dies failing JEDEC
idea: Dies that fail JEDEC sense margin at 85 C are binned (not scrapped) into a datacenter SKU whose controller runs 2x refresh and stronger ECC, with the measured margin written into SPD.
why: Raises usable supply by converting yield loss into product; few-percent more bits per wafer at zero capex.

title: Core-plane diagonal sense wire becomes a noise-reference bitline
idea: Core-memory sense wires ran diagonally so half-select noise from every drive line canceled. Route one dummy bitline per mat diagonally across all bitlines in existing metal, with at most one via-mask change. It picks up the same wordline kick and coupling noise as the real bitlines and serves as a live reference subtracted at each sense-amp group.
why: Removes common-mode wordline-coupling noise ~3x for ~20-30 mV more margin (fact 1), which also allows a lower VARY (fact 10).

title: Capacitive self-bootstrap wordlines eliminate the VPP charge pump
idea: Effect: capacitive bootstrap coupling. Revive the NMOS-era trick: the selected wordline driver's gate node is isolated, then kicked by its own rising output through gate-channel capacitance plus a small MOS cap, lifting the wordline to ~2xVDD for the access with no global VPP pump. Proven by a small team on a mature-node MPW macro.
why: Periphery area/energy (facts 7, 10): removes the VPP pump (~3-5% of die, ~30% efficient) and its grid, cutting activation energy ~20%.

title: Zettacore redox molecules: eight built-in reference levels per cell
idea: Failure mined: Zettacore's porphyrin molecular memory stored charge in discrete oxidation states but died on CMOS process heat and slow voltammetric reads. Fix: after the 400 C steps, graft thermally robust ferrocene/porphyrin mixtures with 7 redox couples onto a nanoporous TiN electrode. The sense amp's reference ladder is a reference electrode coated with the same molecules, so the potential plateaus self-calibrate and each cell stores 3 bits.
why: 10x at the same cost: 3 bits per cell x a crosspoint-compatible 4F^2 footprint (the porous electrode supplies ~50 fF-equivalent charge) x fewer reference generators = ~9-12x vs 1 bit per 6F^2. The molecules cost pennies per wafer.

title: Randomly doped mesowire decoder with post-fab code discovery
idea: From molecular-electronics crossbars: wordlines are addressed through mesowires whose doping pattern is set stochastically by a self-assembled mask, not lithography; after fab a BIST sweeps address codes, finds which code selects each wordline and stores the map in fuses.
why: Row decoders built without fine lithography, losing ~10-20% of code space to unused codes; attacks fact 4 capital and EUV dependence.

title: Toll-road banker: U.S. merchant periphery foundry for bonded DRAM
idea: A banker sees a shared toll road. Build a U.S. merchant foundry that makes only CMOS periphery wafers for bonded DRAM (periphery-under-array, wafer-on-wafer) for every DRAM maker and array startup, who still ship standard DDR5 and HBM.
why: Spreads periphery capex across vendors and brings half of DRAM die function onshore without a full $15B fab (capital, U.S. manufacturability).

title: Self-referenced double sampling cancels sense-amp offset and bitline mismatch
idea: Reverse where the reference comes from: sample the bitline after charge sharing onto capacitor A, write a known '1' through the same cell and sample again onto B, then compare A against B in the same comparator so its offset and the bitline mismatch cancel; restore the true value afterwards (MRAM self-reference transplanted to DRAM).
why: Fact 7: SA transistors can be minimum size because the ~10-20 mV offset cancels; SA area -50-60% and ~30% smaller signals tolerated (smaller Cs), at ~5 ns extra read latency.

title: Local quality: graded-threshold tiers replace the 3D staircase decoder
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: each tier of a 3D stack is deposited with its own in-situ doping so its select-transistor pair (one n-type, one p-type in series) has thresholds stepped ~150 mV per tier, forming a voltage window; a single vertical gate rod driven by one precision DAC level opens exactly one tier, with no staircase contact etch.
why: 100x path: deletes the staircase (~10-20% of 3D die area and dozens of trim/etch steps) so tiers can scale cheaply; trade-offs: threshold control limits each window band to ~16-32 tiers, and selection is slower. Attacks Facts 2, 4 and 7.

title: Bond array-only wafers to US mature-node periphery wafers
idea: Box: 1T1C x vertical-channel access x SA on a separate wafer x wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding at ~0.4 um pitch x two Si substrates x US 22-28 nm foundry. The memory fab builds pure arrays with no periphery or HV devices, and an existing U.S. logic foundry builds all SAs, decoders and pumps on a second wafer bonded face-to-face per bitline group.
why: Capital and U.S. manufacturability: periphery's ~49% moves to depreciated U.S. fabs; array die area ~-40%, DRAM-fab capex per bit down, domestic content up.

title: Lost-foam casting: sacrificial polymer evaporates into bitline air gaps
idea: Like lost-foam casting, where the foam pattern vaporizes as metal fills the mold, fill between bitlines with a thermally decomposable polynorbornene (late-1990s chemistry) and cap it with porous oxide. A ~425 C bake makes the polymer diffuse out, leaving air gaps.
why: Cuts bitline-to-bitline capacitance ~40% and total bitline capacitance ~20-30%: ~1.3x more signal (fewer SA strips, ~3-4% die) or a ~25% smaller capacitor.

title: Ca: calcium-titanate varactor parametrically pumps bitline signal up
idea: Add a CaTiO3 paraelectric varactor to each bitline; after charge sharing, the sense-enable pulse biases it to drop its capacitance 3-4x, so the same signal charge appears as a 3-4x larger voltage before a smaller, less-matched latch fires.
why: Raises effective signal without more Cs (fact 1) and relaxes SA offset matching so SA transistors shrink, cutting SA area ~30-50% (fact 7).

title: Po: gate from underneath — Hf-free back-gated FD-SOI periphery
idea: Po: transistors controlled from underneath. Build the periphery on thin-BOX FD-SOI with SiON front gates and TiN or doped-poly electrodes (no HfO2), using the back gate through the buried oxide for Vt control, and give each SA pair its own back-gate island biased to null its offset.
why: Scarce resources and capacitor wall (#1): avoids hafnium while recovering Vt tuning via body bias; per-SA back-bias trim cuts required signal; Si, O, N, Ti only.

title: Liquid-metal capsules self-heal broken vertical interconnects
idea: Ideal result: a broken wire that rejoins itself. Fill spare vias beside TSVs and bitline contacts with encapsulated Ga-In micro-capsules that rupture from the local heat of a forming void and wick into the crack, restoring continuity.
why: TSV yield (fact 6) and lifetime reliability: converts open-circuit failures into self-repairs.

title: Analog syndrome bitlines compute parity by charge summation in-array
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x multi-level analog-sum sensing x dedicated parity bitline x bulk Si x standard. During activation, cells of a parity group also dump charge onto a shared parity bitline; a small multi-level comparator turns the summed charge into a count whose mod-2 is the syndrome, so only words with a nonzero syndrome go to the full decoder.
why: Decoder power and latency at 1% BER: most words skip decoding; periphery ECC logic ~-50%.

title: One sense amp resolves four bitlines in sequence
idea: Inverting 'one sense amp per bitline pair': four bitline pairs charge-share simultaneously, are isolated, and hold their analog signals while a single sense amp resolves and restores them one after another in ~2 ns slots.
why: Sense-amp count -75%, freeing ~10-15% die area for a few ns of activation time; risk is signal decay and coupling during the hold.

title: Noise-cancelling headphone loop on the cell plate
idea: Borrowed from active noise cancellation and ECG driven-right-leg amplifiers: dummy bitlines in each mat pick up common-mode noise (plate bounce, wordline kick, substrate), and a fast amplifier drives the inverse onto the plate and reference lines during sensing.
why: Sensing margin: removes ~10-20 mV of correlated noise (~25% of today's budget), allowing smaller Cs or longer bitlines.

title: Inkjet-printed personality layer turns one die into many SKUs
idea: Worse: tape out separate masks and dies for each width, density bin and speed grade. Flip: leave the final configuration via layer unpatterned and inkjet-print jumpers per wafer to set I/O width, bank grouping, redundancy and timing options, so one mask set serves the whole product line.
why: Capital intensity (masks) and supply agility: fabs shift output between products in days instead of quarters.

title: Single-poly floating-gate CAM stores repair addresses without fuses
idea: Effect: Fowler-Nordheim tunneling onto a floating gate. In a standard-logic MPW macro, repair and trim addresses live in single-poly floating-gate cells programmed through the thin gate oxide with no extra masks, arranged as a CAM that compares incoming row addresses directly. No laser fuses, no boot-time fuse broadcast, and field re-programmable for post-package repair.
why: Periphery area/yield (fact 7): fuse banks (~2% of die) removed and in-field repair raises effective yield; zero added mask cost suits a fabless team.

title: Equipotentiality: clamped motionless bitlines with charge-transfer sensing
idea: TRIZ #12 Equipotentiality: each bitline is held at a constant potential by a cascode clamp; the cell's charge flows through the clamp onto a ~0.5 fF sense node, amplified by the capacitance ratio, and restore injects charge back through the same clamp, so the large bitline never swings.
why: Facts 5, 8 and 10: bitline swing energy (~60% of activation energy) drops ~10x and bitline-to-bitline coupling noise nearly vanishes.

title: Constant-weight coding with winner-take-half rank sensing
idea: Inverting 'a reference must come from a dummy cell or twin bitline': rows store data in a constant-weight code (exactly 8 ones per 16-cell group), and a winner-take-half circuit declares the 8 highest bitlines of each group to be ones, so no reference voltage exists at all.
why: Removes reference/dummy circuitry, is immune to common-mode drift and leakage, and tolerates ~2x smaller signals for robust open-bitline 4F^2 sensing, at ~15% code overhead.

title: Per-subarray micro-ring modulators replace global data lines
idea: Inverting 'data leaves the bank on copper': a silicon-nitride waveguide layer in the top BEOL runs over every subarray, each subarray's local sense output drives a micro-ring modulator on its own wavelength, and 32 subarrays share one waveguide by WDM to the package edge.
why: Replaces global I/O lines and repeaters (a large share of periphery power); targets <1 pJ/bit data movement vs 3-20 pJ/bit today.

title: EUV-free decoder: coarse mesowires plus stochastic doping and lookup map
idea: Limit: no EUV or immersion patterning in decoder transistors. Borrowing nanowire-crossbar decoders, a few coarse i-line address wires cross the dense wordline ends, and graded implant or gate-oxide thickness gives each wordline a unique threshold code; a post-fab BIST pass maps logical rows to the physical codes that actually work and stores the map in a few kb.
why: Litho/capital (fact 4): pitch-matched decoder/driver strips are among the hardest periphery patterns; using cheap i-line plus calibration could drop 1-2 critical masks and cut decoder area ~30%.

title: Kerf-resident BIST and test modes sawn off after sort
idea: Place BIST engines, test-mode decoders and probe-only analog monitors in the scribe lanes, wired across the kerf to each die; they run at wafer sort and are physically discarded at dicing, leaving only a lockout fuse on the die.
why: Periphery (fact 7): test circuitry is ~3-5% of die area; reclaiming it gives ~3-5% more dies per wafer on existing lines at zero capex.

title: Po: contacts made of silicon itself — silicide-capped epi plugs
idea: Po: a contact with no tungsten. Fill periphery contacts with in-situ-doped selective epitaxial silicon capped by self-aligned TiSi2/NiSi, topped by a TiN/Al local layer, eliminating WF6 CVD tungsten plugs throughout the periphery.
why: Scarce resources: removes tungsten (China ~80%) from contacts using Si, Ti, Ni, N, Al; epi plugs also tighten contact-resistance spread.

title: Bitline capped at 10 fF: segment amplifiers inside the array tier
idea: Limit: no bitline may exceed 10 fF. Every 32 cells, a 2-transistor local amplifier (gate on the local bitline, drain on a global bitline) is built in the same vertical-channel tier as the access transistors, turning charge sharing into current gain on a global line.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): with a 4x smaller C_BL, Cs can drop to ~1.5-2 fF (planar or low-AR capacitors), which unblocks the 3D DRAM capacitor (fact 2).

title: Soft-decision dual-time latch sampling feeds on-die LDPC
idea: Substitute the hard binary sense decision with soft information: each latch output is sampled at an early and a late strobe, and disagreement flags a low-confidence bit. An on-die soft-decision LDPC over 512-bit column words then corrects them.
why: Charge wall and refresh (facts 1, 3): tolerating ~2x lower signal margin allows Cs ~3 fF instead of 5 fF, or 2-4x longer refresh intervals.

title: Row decoders built from the array's own vertical transistors
idea: Inverting 'decoders are CMOS logic in the periphery': predecoded NAND-style row selection is made from series vertical-channel transistors fabricated in the same steps as the cell access devices and placed at the mat edge at cell pitch, replacing the per-mat CMOS decoder/driver stripe.
why: Shrinks the decoder/wordline-driver stripe ~50-70% (several % of die) and removes CMOS mask steps from the DRAM wafer.

title: Wavelength-coded optical row decoding with microring drop filters
idea: Substitute the electrical row decoder tree with wavelength selection: an on-die SiN waveguide carries one of N laser lines, a microring drop filter tuned to each row group routes it to a photodiode, and the photodiode triggers that group's local wordline driver. The address is the wavelength.
why: Periphery area and energy: removes multi-stage NAND decode trees and long address buses (~8-10% of die) and makes decode energy nearly independent of array size.

title: Darkroom dodge-and-burn: per-mat precharge level trimmed at test
idea: Like a printer dodging and burning areas of a photograph, measure each mat's '0' and '1' bitline signal distributions at wafer sort. Then program a 4-bit offset on that mat's precharge voltage with 1990s laser-fuse repair tools, so the reference sits midway between the real, leakage-skewed distributions.
why: Leakage pulls stored '1's down asymmetrically; re-centering recovers ~20-30% of margin, which becomes ~1.5-2x longer refresh intervals or a smaller capacitor.

title: Honeycomb: brick-bond mat tiling shares each sense strip three ways
idea: Bees get the most area per wall with hexagons. Lay mats in a Manhattan-friendly brick-bond pattern that approximates hexagons so each SA strip segment borders three mats, and give each SA 3:1 isolation switches; only one of the three mats is active per strip at a time, versus 2:1 sharing today.
why: Periphery area: SA strips are ~20-25% of die; three-way sharing removes ~1/3 of SAs per bit, ~7% die area saved, at the cost of activation constraints between neighbouring mats.

title: Charlieplexed wordlines with thin-film bidirectional selectors
idea: Borrowed from LED charlieplexing: wordlines are selected by ordered pairs of N driver lines through back-to-back oxide Schottky-diode selectors on glass, so N drivers address N(N-1) rows (32 drivers select 992 rows).
why: Periphery: row-driver count per mat down ~30x, which matters on glass where thin-film drivers are large.

title: CCD bucket-brigade column shifts charge to one amplifier
idea: Borrowed from astronomical CCDs: in streaming banks, clocked gates along each column shift every cell's charge packet down to a single floating-diffusion source follower at the column end instead of dumping it onto a heavy bitline. The packet arrives undivided, so the signal is Cs/Cfd instead of Cs/Cbl.
why: Charge wall: signal gain ~20-50x versus charge sharing, permitting sub-fF cells; fits sequential AI weight streaming at ~1 ns per shift stage.

title: SerDes decision-feedback equalizer cancels bitline crosstalk
idea: Borrowed from high-speed SerDes DFE: sense amps fire in two staggered phases, and the decided values of phase-1 neighbors feed back through small programmed coupling capacitors to subtract their known crosstalk from phase-2 bitlines. Open-bitline arrays can then run at minimum pitch without dummy reference mats or twisting.
why: Density and periphery: removes the ~3-5% die area of edge dummy mats and lets bitline pitch tighten ~15% at the same F.

title: Eliminate high-k metal-gate periphery: slow, wide internal buses with poly/SiON
idea: Make the internal datapath 8x wider at 1/8 the clock (a 4,096-bit, 400 MHz bonded port), so periphery transistors can be plain poly-Si/SiON at 65-90 nm-class speed. Gates are etched with HBr/Cl2 and spacers are Al2O3 etched with BCl3, removing gate-last HKMG, dual work-function metals and their fluorinated steps.
why: Periphery masks -4-6 and steps ~-20%, buildable on legacy U.S. tools; wide-slow I/O also cuts interface energy ~3x (fact 5).

title: Zn: zinc-oxide thin-film varistors shrink I/O ESD clamps
idea: Replace bulky diode/SCR ESD clamps at each DQ and CA pad with a Bi/Mn-doped sol-gel ZnO varistor film in the pad stack, whose grain-boundary breakdown gives strongly nonlinear clamping and absorbs surge energy in volume, not die area.
why: Frees ~3-5% of die area in I/O periphery and lowers pad capacitance ~30%, which reduces I/O energy per bit (fact 5).

title: Compressed-sensing reads via random multi-row current sums
idea: Inverting 'each bit is sensed individually': in capacitorless FeFET NOR columns, 16 random-pattern wordline combinations are activated and the summed bitline currents go to a 4-bit ADC, from which sparse 64-cell groups (mostly zeros, as in activations and zero pages) are reconstructed.
why: Up to ~4x fewer sense operations and less I/O energy for sparse data; dense groups fall back to normal reads.

title: Detector physicist's charge amplifier: virtual-ground bitlines grab all charge
idea: Silicon-strip detectors read femtocoulombs with a charge-sensitive amplifier that holds the electrode at virtual ground. A feedback amplifier (shared by 4-8 bitlines through a mux) holds the bitline fixed so the whole cell charge lands on a ~1 fF feedback capacitor instead of sharing with ~50 fF of bitline.
why: Transfer ratio rises from ~0.1 to ~0.9, a 5-10x larger signal: ~1 fF cells without tall pillars, or 4x longer bitlines (facts 1, 2, 7).

title: Seashell roar: chopped, dithered comparator voting senses sub-offset signals
idea: A seashell turns random noise into a perceptible 'ocean': use stochastic resonance. After charge sharing, sample the bitline onto a small isolated cap, then fire a minimum-size comparator 8 times against a reference dithered by an on-die junction-noise source, swapping inputs on alternate firings (chopping) to cancel offset, and majority-vote in a 3-bit counter before restore.
why: Sense-amp area: minimum-size comparators with ~30 mV offset can resolve ~10 mV signals statistically, so SA transistors shrink ~4x in area (SA strips are a large share of the ~49% periphery), at a cost of ~2-3 ns latency.

title: Diffusion-furnace bipolar sense amps: BiCMOS revival for millivolt signals
idea: Like a batch furnace that dopes thousands of wafers identically, bipolar transistors match by diffusion depth and emitter area rather than gate litho. Use 1990s BiCMOS to put bipolar differential pre-amps (Vbe mismatch ~0.5 mV) ahead of CMOS latches, shared across column groups.
why: ~10x lower offset than MOS pairs lets bitlines carry 4-8x more cells, or lets a ~1 fF planar capacitor work, so a 180 nm U.S. fab could make dense-enough memory without deep trenches.

title: Permanent-mold sense amps: ferroelectric gate nulls each amplifier's offset forever
idea: Like a permanent metal mold that is set once and reused for thousands of castings, give one transistor of each SA input pair an HZO ferroelectric gate layer. At wafer test a binary search programs its polarization to cancel that SA's measured offset, and it stays trimmed for life with no fuse area.
why: Residual offset falls from ~15-20 mV sigma to ~3-5 mV, so bitline signal can drop ~3x: 2-3x longer bitlines (SA strip area -50%) or Cs reduced to ~2 fF.

title: Genetic-programming evolved sense-amp netlists proven on SkyWater 130 shuttle
idea: Sense-amp netlists are treated as genomes and evolved by mutation and recombination in open-source SPICE on cloud CPUs, selecting for Monte-Carlo offset, area and energy. The top 10 survivors tape out on an open SkyWater 130 shuttle next to a classic latch. Compute $100k plus shuttle/test $150k plus 2 engineers, ~$750k in 24 months.
why: Fact 1/7: may find sense amps with ~30% less area or 2x lower offset per area, licensable to DRAM makers.

title: Alien's 'not sure' bit: confidence-tagged sensing feeds erasure ECC
idea: An alien answers yes, no or not sure. Each SA group gets a resolution-time detector: a latch slower than a threshold to resolve flags its bit as an erasure, and the on-die ECC decoder switches to erasure decoding, which fixes about twice as many flagged errors as blind ones.
why: Doubles the effective error budget of the existing on-die ECC, buying ~30% less cell charge or longer bitlines (facts 1, 7) with no interface change.

title: Balanced-code words generate their own mid-level sense reference
idea: Encode each 64-bit word as a 68-bit constant-weight code (exactly 34 ones), so the average of the word's own bitlines is exactly halfway between its decayed '1' and '0' levels. A charge-sharing copy of the word's bitlines becomes the SA reference, tracking leakage at 125 C automatically.
why: Cells can decay much further before failure: ~2-4x longer refresh at hot for 6% bit overhead (fact 3).

title: Core-rope weaving: diode-matrix row decoder with no PMOS
idea: Like Apollo's core-rope memory, where each wire threaded through or around a core encoded a bit, encode each wordline's address by placing or omitting a Schottky diode where it crosses the predecoded lines (one implant mask at 180 nm). The result is a dynamic diode-AND decoder.
why: Diodes are ~4x smaller than a CMOS NAND stack and need no well spacing: decoder area -50-60%, buildable at i-line rules.

title: Negative-capacitance ferroelectric gate on sense-amp input pair
idea: Scale molecule-level dipole switching up into the sense path: a thin doped-HfO2 negative-capacitance layer in the gate stack of the SA input transistors gives ~2-3x internal voltage gain on the 50-100 mV charge-shared bitline signal before the latch fires.
why: More effective signal per femtocoulomb lets Cs drop ~2x or bitlines lengthen ~2x (facts 1, 7) and relaxes SA offset sizing.

title: N-type-only oxide sense amp using capacitive bootstrapping
idea: MINIFY the device menu to one transistor type: an IGZO-only cross-coupled latch uses bootstrapped capacitive pull-ups (as in display gate drivers) instead of p-FETs, avoiding immature p-type oxides and keeping the periphery tier to ~8 masks at <=350 C.
why: Facts 4 and 7: a mask-light, EUV-free periphery tier above the array; ~2-3x slower than Si SAs, offset by sensing more columns in parallel.

title: Equivalent-time sampling scope built into each sense stripe
idea: 1960s sampling oscilloscopes captured GHz waveforms by sampling repeated events at slipping delays. Add one sampling switch and comparator per sense stripe; across repeated activations it reconstructs the real bitline charge-sharing waveform, and boot firmware sets each mat's tRCD and sense-enable timing from it.
why: Removes worst-case timing guardbands: ~15-25% lower tRCD/tRAS and better yield of slow mats (facts 1, 4).

title: Write-once AI weights move to a 3D antifuse ROM tier
idea: Failure mined: Matrix Semiconductor's 3D one-time-programmable diode/antifuse memory was dense and cheap but found no market for write-once bits. Fix: frozen inference weights are exactly that market. Program them into 8-deck 3D antifuse crosspoints with a DRAM-class read path (short bitlines, 40 ns random read), freeing HBM and DRAM for KV cache and activations.
why: 10x at the same cost: 8 decks x 4F^2 = ~12x DRAM bits/mm^2 with no capacitor, refresh or write path. Weights are 50-80% of inference DRAM demand, so the DRAM bought per deployed model falls 2-5x.

title: Eliminate the switched-capacitor charge pump: on-die piezoelectric AlN transformer
idea: Replace each bank's VPP pump with a solidly mounted Rosen-type AlN piezoelectric transformer (~200 um, ~25 MHz resonance) that steps 1.1 V up to ~3 V at ~80% efficiency into a diode rectifier. AlN is sputtered and etched with Cl2/BCl3, and its Mo electrodes with Cl2/O2, with no release etch.
why: Pumps take ~3-5% of area at 30-40% efficiency, so VPP energy roughly halves and the large MOS pump capacitors go away (facts 7 and 10).

title: Strowger stepper: token-passing wordline drivers replace local row decoders
idea: A Strowger telephone switch steps one contact per pulse instead of decoding a full number. For streaming and AI traffic that walks rows in order, make each wordline driver a bootstrapped 4-transistor dynamic shift stage (as in LCD gate-on-array drivers) passing a single token, and keep a coarse random-access decoder only every 32 rows to jump the token.
why: Periphery area (fact 7): removes the row-address bus and per-row NAND decode from the local driver strip, perhaps 20-30% of decoder area; random jumps cost up to 31 extra clock steps, acceptable for sequential tiers.

title: HBM base die absorbs all core-die periphery
idea: Make HBM core dies array-only (cells plus wordline straps), hybrid-bond each one face-to-face to a logic-process periphery tier holding the SAs and decoders, and merge the base-die functions into the same periphery design, so the duplicate IO and TSV drivers on each core die disappear.
why: Periphery 49% (fact 7) and HBM TSV tax (fact 6): array efficiency ~50% to ~85% (~1.6x bits per array wafer), with lower-power logic-process SAs.

title: Blessing in disguise: random sense amp offsets form a reference ladder
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: a bank of 8 tiny unequalized latches per 64 bitlines samples each held bitline voltage in turn; their natural random offsets (sigma ~15 mV), measured once at test, act as a free reference ladder, so the pattern of which latches flip gives 2-3 bits of soft information or multilevel reads with no reference generators.
why: Density and reliability: soft-read information for ECC or 2-bit cells without reference circuitry; mismatch, normally Fact 7's area driver, becomes the resource.

title: Child's tidy toy box: refresh skips rows holding only safe values
idea: A child knows toys already on the floor cannot fall. During refresh the SA stripe computes a wired-OR of bits stored in the leak-vulnerable charged state (using the die's own true/anti-cell map); rows with none, common for zeroed pages, are flagged in an on-die bitmap and skipped until next written.
why: Zeroed and sparse pages are often 20-40% of memory; skipping them cuts refresh energy proportionally (fact 3) with no controller change.

title: Po: wordlines count themselves — analog hammer integrator cell
idea: Po: a wordline that keeps its own tally. Each sub-wordline driver gets one extra DRAM-style cell coupled to its wordline through a tiny capacitor so every activation deposits a fixed charge quantum; when that integrator crosses a threshold during the row group's refresh, its neighbors are flagged for targeted refresh and the integrator is reset.
why: Row hammer (#9) at ~1k activations: exact per-row counting at roughly one cell per row instead of SRAM counter tables or controller tracking, and it keeps working as thresholds fall further.

title: Test brains live in the probe card, not every die
idea: Reverse where DFT lives: test-mode logic, BIST engines, compression and burn-in controllers are stripped from the DRAM die and implemented once on an ASIC in a U.S.-made probe card, reaching the array through a thin raw-access port.
why: Fact 7: ~2-4% die area recovered on every die; test logic is amortized over millions of dies and upgradable without a respin.

title: Band-to-band tunneling FET sense amplifier enables 0.4 V array voltage
idea: Effect: band-to-band (Zener) tunneling. Build the SA cross-coupled pair from vertical Ge/Si heterojunction TFETs with ~30 mV/dec turn-on, so the latch regenerates with only 0.4 V across it; complementary n/p TFET pairs handle their one-way conduction.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): VARY falls from ~1 V to 0.4 V, so bitline CV^2 energy drops ~6x for activation and refresh.

title: Eliminate fluorinated test fluids: self-heating hammer-pattern thermal screening
idea: Hot test and burn-in normally rely on PFPE (Galden/Fluorinert) chillers and baths. Instead each die heats itself to 95-125 C with an all-bank activate pattern (~1-2 W), closed-loop on an on-die ring-oscillator thermometer, so handlers need only air-cooled chucks and retention screens run at true temperature.
why: Removes PFAS heat-transfer fluids from test floors and cuts handler capex ~30%; the pattern also screens hammer-weak rows (fact 9).

title: Igloo: 77 K memory tier runs sensing at half voltage
idea: Keep memory cold like an igloo: put a capacity-tier DRAM in a liquid-nitrogen bath at 77 K, where access-transistor leakage falls by orders of magnitude (refresh nearly vanishes), wire resistance drops ~5x and threshold voltages can be retargeted, so VARY runs at ~0.5 V and VPP at ~1.5 V with periphery at 0.4 V.
why: CV2 terms fall ~4x, wordline ~4x, refresh ~100x, and lower wire resistance shrinks drivers; net ~10x per access at the device even after amortized cryocooler overhead at data-centre scale is debated.

title: Photoreceptor light adaptation: reference voltage tracking time since refresh
idea: Like a photoreceptor shifting its operating point with ambient light, a per-bank reference generator walks the sense reference down the expected charge-loss curve since that row group's last refresh. A drooped '1' is then still compared against a threshold midway between the decayed '1' and the '0'.
why: Fact 3: a fixed mid-rail reference fails a '1' at VDD/2. A tracking reference roughly doubles the allowable droop, extending tREFW 1.5-2.5x and cutting refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit) and the 10-20% bandwidth tax in proportion.

title: Model T periphery: sense amps from the array transistor only
idea: Ford's Model T came in one colour to cut production steps. Design every pitch-matched periphery circuit (SAs, sub-wordline drivers, column switches) from the buried-channel array transistor plus one thick-oxide variant, using bootstrapped gates and NMOS-only latches with capacitive pull-up instead of a separate HKMG CMOS periphery module.
why: Water: deleting the periphery HKMG module (~8-12 masks, ~40 wet cleans and strips) cuts that module's water >10x and total fab water ~20%; mask and EUV counts fall too.

title: Single-electron transistor electrometer senses attofarad cells
idea: Borrow spin-qubit readout: couple a silicon single-electron transistor capacitively to each micro-cell storage node and read it by RF reflectometry with frequency multiplexing, so cells storing only ~100 electrons can be read.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): Cs ~50x smaller (~0.02 fF), allowing planar cells and many cheap 3D tiers (fact 2); needs room-temperature SET operation, which is very hard.

title: Fund U.S. roll-to-roll advanced-packaging lines for memory periphery layers
idea: Worse: leave printed and laminated packaging layers to offshore suppliers so every module ships through Asia. Flip: CHIPS-style grants and offtake guarantees for U.S. roll-to-roll lines making organic interposers, decap laminates and printed repair and configuration layers for domestic memory assembly.
why: U.S. manufacturability: printed lines cost ~$50-200M versus $15B fabs and onshore the periphery and packaging share of memory value.

title: Moth-ear minimal-periphery eDRAM compiler for open U.S. PDKs
idea: Noctuid moths detect bats with ears of just two neurons. An open-source compiler for SkyWater 130/GF180 generates 3T gain-cell eDRAM macros with radically minimal periphery: single-ended inverter sensing, shared counter refresh and standard-cell decoders. Two shuttles validate it for ~$700k in 24 months.
why: U.S. manufacturability: gives domestic mature-node fabs a working-memory macro ~2-3x denser than SRAM for chiplets now, seeding a U.S. DRAM design base.

title: Segmented cell-plate kick boosts read signal before charge sharing
idea: Worse: hold the cell plate at a static VDD/2 so the signal is only what Cs alone delivers. Flip: split the plate into per-mat segments and pulse the selected mat's plate by a few hundred mV during the read to couple extra charge onto the bitline, then return it before restore.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): ~20-30% more signal from the same ~5 fF, buying aspect-ratio relief or longer bitlines.

title: Roll-to-roll conductive-elastomer probe film for full-wafer parallel test
idea: Worse: test DRAM with costly MEMS probe cards a few dies at a time and pack extra test logic onto every die. Flip: use a disposable roll-to-roll-printed anisotropic conductive-elastomer film that contacts every pad on the wafer at once, fanned out through a printed flex to the tester.
why: Test cost and test-periphery area: full-wafer parallelism lowers test cost per bit and the on-die test-compression logic needed.

title: Eliminate the sense amplifier via negative-capacitance bitlines
idea: Put a thin ferroelectric HZO layer in series between each bitline and its parasitic shield, biased so its negative capacitance cancels ~60% of bitline capacitance. The charge-share signal rises from ~100 mV to ~300 mV, enough for a plain skewed-inverter pair instead of a matched latch.
why: SA offset-matching area goes away (SA -40%), or Cs can drop 2-3x at the same margin, attacking the capacitor charge wall (fact 1). Negative-capacitance stability and hysteresis are unproven.

title: Resonant-capacitance read of varactor cells, after RCA's CED stylus
idea: Failure mined: RCA's Capacitance Electronic Disc read its signal as capacitance shifts in a 915 MHz resonant circuit, but its contact stylus wore out. Fix without contact: the storage node is the gate of a MOS varactor, and the cell is read by the resonant-frequency shift of a short bitline LC tank at a few GHz. The read draws no charge from the node, so no restore is needed.
why: Destructive read and restore (fact 8): removes write-back energy, so the same row can be re-read at ~1/3 the energy, and row-hammer exposure falls because reads stop disturbing neighbors.
